canonical_question: What specific 'deformation mechanisms' are hypothesized to occur at room temperature versus high temperatures in the SLM-built alloy?

question_variants.question: What specific 'deformation mechanisms' are hypothesized to occur at room temperature versus high temperatures in the SLM-built alloy?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper identifies slip and deformation twins as the main deformation mechanisms from 25 °C to 600 °C. It mentions an attempt to identify room- and high-temperature deformation mechanisms and infers high-temperature properties are due to high dislocation density and fine precipitates, but does not explicitly name the specific mechanism for temperatures above 600 °C (e.g., creep) in the provided evidence spans.

answers.answer: The main deformation mechanisms from 25 °C to 600 °C are identified as slip and deformation twins. For high temperatures (700 °C or higher), the text infers properties are achieved with high dislocation density and fine precipitates but does not explicitly name the specific mechanism (e.g., dislocation climb, diffusion) for the high-temp range in the provided spans.
answers.conditions: 25 °C to 600 °C (room to moderate) and 700 °C or higher (high temp)
answers.measurement_outcome: Deformation mechanisms observed as slip and deformation twins for 25-600 °C.
answers.mechanism: Slip and deformation twins (25-600 °C); High dislocation density and fine precipitates support properties at 700 °C+.
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific high-temperature deformation mechanism name (beyond microstructural support features) not explicitly stated for >600 °C.
evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present.
